title: How Blest the Righteous Are
description: How Blest the Righteous Are in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 20, “Balaam's wish Num 23:10”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How blest the right-eous are When they re-sign their breath! No won-der Bal-aam wished to share In such a hap-py death.

lines: No wonder Balaam wished to share
When life is ended let me be
The force of truth how great!
None but the righteous whom they hate,
He seemed the Lord to know,
For none can serve them both.
May you, my friends, and I,
If like the righteous we would die,
To choose the life they live.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
